office.name: Center for Religion, Spirituality, and Social Justice (CRSSJ)
office.quote: The Center for Religion, Spirituality and Social Justice (CRSSJ) is a place on campus to ask big questions, receive emotional and spiritual support, connect with community and ensure your religious and spiritual needs are met during your time at Grinnell.

communities.name: Shared Table: Wednesday Dinners and Conversation
communities.quote: Join the community and Rev. Cassandra each week for homemade dinner and thoughtful conversation as we explore what it means to think critically and live faithfully as Christians.

communities.name: Chapel at Grinnell College
communities.quote: Join us during the academic year for Christian worship. Services are at 10:30 a.m. in Herrick Chapel.

communities.name: Catholic Students Association (CSA)
communities.quote: Join a group of students interested in maintaining or rediscovering their Catholic faith through meeting other Catholic students, discussing important issues surrounding the church, and participating in volunteer activities.

communities.name: Chaverim
communities.quote: Join Chaverim and Rabbi Sarah Brammer-Shlay when school is in session for Shabbat Table. In addition to Shabbat, there are many opportunities to gather as a Jewish community throughout the year.

communities.name: Grinnell Meditation
communities.quote: During the academic year, we offer a weekly meditation sit on Mondays at 8:30 p.m. at the CRSSJ with Jordan Scheibel '10.

communities.name: Hindu Culture and Sanatana Dharma (HCSD)
communities.quote: The new in-progress Hindu Culture and Sanatana Dharma (HCSD) group meets within the space and provides a place for students to gather and engage in group pujas (worship), prepare prasad and satvik foods (for prayer and religious observance), sing bhajans (devotional songs), study Hindu texts such as the Bhagavad Gita, or just learn more about the practices of sanatana dharma.

communities.name: Muslim Student Association (MSA)
communities.quote: Grinnell College Center for Religion, Spirituality, and Social Justice has a Muslim prayer room available for students to use during the academic year.

communities.name: Quaker Friends Silent Meeting
communities.quote: The Grinnell Quaker Worship Group meets in the silent tradition of the Religious Society of Friends in which worshippers use the collective silence, broken occasionally by "vocal ministry," to open themselves up to spiritual guidance and insight.

communities.name: Multi-Faith
communities.quote: Join our Chaplains in a lively and communal discussion of religion and personal perspectives regarding theories and practices of religious traditions.

communities.name: Secular community
communities.quote: If you are interested in joining an intentional secular community, please email Rev. Cassandra Lawrence who is supporting students who identify as secular, humanist, atheist, agnostic, or other language to find spaces to gather and be together.

communities.name: Chaverim: Jewish Student Organization
communities.quote: Chaverim provides a Jewish community on Grinnell's campus. We seek to promote Jewish life through various religious, cultural, and social events open to both Jewish and non-Jewish students as well as Jewish faculty and community members.
